article.chapter: Tópico, sujeto y contraste: は/が — 主題・主語・対比：は／が

claims.summary: Tahara and Ito (1985) report an elicited picture-story study in which adults and the 14-year-old group systematically differentiated wa and ga by discourse function, with younger groups showing gradual development; the result is scoped to their task and is not a universal first-mention rule.

The study included 90 participants aged four through adulthood and elicited stories from picture sequences; its old/new characterization is treated as a discourse pattern under the study task, with age and narrative context affecting the distribution.

Amano (1998) describes three focus configurations in ga noun-predicate sentences (focus before ga, after ga, or across the sentence) and argues against reducing ga to a single focus-marker function; contextual interpretation is required.
